samples.summary: Cleared colour key stays present-with-undefined in the in-memory block but is deleted from the CRDT, so a colour reset inside a named style (heading/subtitle) renders differently in-session than after reload or on a peer
samples.evidence: `applyInlineStyle` merges `{ ...inline.style, ...resolvedStyle }` (block-helpers.ts:348) where `resolvedStyle.color === undefined`. `normalizeInlines` copies that style verbatim (`{...inline.style}`, block-helpers.ts:84), so whenever the cleared slice is the first surviving run (e.g. clearing over the whole block, or offset 0) the block cached by the store keeps `color: undefined` AS A PRESENT KEY. `view/layout.ts:156` computes `{ ...defaults, ...inline.style }`, and a present `undefined` overrides the named-style default — so a heading-3/subtitle/heading-6 run (named-style `color: '#434343'`/'#666666', named-styles.ts:85-91) paints the fallback (black) locally. The Yorkie path instead REMOVES the attribute (`removedInlineStyleAttrs` → `removeStyleByPath`, yorkie-doc-store.ts:1880-1886) and `parseInlineStyle` only sets `color` when `'color' in attrs` (line 177), so after a reload — or for any peer — the key is absent and the named-style colour reappears. Before this change both cache and CRDT stored `''` and rendered consistently; the fix introduces the divergence. The new Yorkie tests cannot see it because `reread` builds a fresh store from the tree (tests/app/docs/yorkie-doc-store.test.ts:599).

samples.summary: Table-cell background "Reset" still writes the dead empty-string colour the fix removes for inline runs — it bypasses normalizeStyleClears entirely
samples.evidence: `editor.applyTableCellStyle({ backgroundColor: "" })` (docs-table-context-menu.tsx:230) writes into `CellStyle.backgroundColor` (model/types.ts:470), a path that never reaches `normalizeStyleClears` (only `applyInlineStyle`/`applyStyleInTree` call it). The result is exactly the state issue #793 describes for inline runs: an empty-string colour stored on the cell that is falsy for painters (`if (!cell.style?.backgroundColor) continue`, export/pdf-table-painter.ts:173) but is still a present key/attribute for anything treating presence as "has a fill".

samples.summary: No read-side/migration normalization: runs already persisted with backgroundColor:'' or color:'' keep the dead value forever
samples.evidence: `normalizeStyleClears` only inspects the incoming patch. Documents written before this change already contain `backgroundColor: ''` on runs; on load `parseInlineStyle` keeps it (`if ('backgroundColor' in attrs)`, yorkie-doc-store.ts:178) and `inlineStylesEqual`/`storedColorsEqual` still treat `''` ≠ unset (model/types.ts:446), so those runs can never re-merge and still look like "there is a highlight" to presence-based consumers. Applying an unrelated style later (e.g. `{bold:true}`) does not heal them either, because the existing run style is spread through untouched.
searchedFor: grep for migration/normalize on document load in packages/docs/src/store

verdict.reason: Every claimed link in the chain checks out in the repository. normalizeStyleClears deliberately produces a key PRESENT with value `undefined` (packages/docs/src/model/types.ts:277-286, documented at 267-268), and applyInlineStyle spreads that into the styled slice (`{ ...inline.style, ...resolvedStyle }`, block-helpers.ts:348). normalizeInlines preserves it via `{ ...inline.style }` (block-helpers.ts:84) — object spread copies own keys even when the value is undefined — and inlineStylesEqual treats undefined==absent (types.ts:445), so when the cleared slice is the first surviving run the merged style keeps `color: undefined`. Layout then merges named-style defaults UNDER the inline style (`{ ...defaults, ...inline.style }`, view/layout.ts:156), so the present-undefined key shadows the named-style colour (`#434343` for heading-3, `#666666` for subtitle/heading-4/5/6, named-styles.ts:85-91) and paint falls back to Theme.defaultColor (view/paint-layout.ts:385, view/table-renderer.ts:457) — i.e. black locally. The CRDT path instead REMOVES the attribute (removedInlineStyleAttrs + tree.removeStyleByPath, yorkie-doc-store.ts:1878-1886), and parseInlineStyle only sets color when `'color' in attrs` (yorkie-doc-store.ts:177, backend/docs-tree.ts:114), so after reload or on a peer the key is absent and the named-style colour reappears. The cache is what renders in-session: getDocument returns cachedDoc while !dirty (yorkie-doc-store.ts:545-546) and applyStyle sets the cache from applyInlineStyleHelper then clears dirty (yorkie-doc-store.ts:1708,1721-1723). No guard strips undefined-valued keys after the merge — cloneBlock's JSON round-trip happens before it (block-helpers.ts:326). Real, in-lane (incorrect rendered state, cache/CRDT state inconsistency), non-trivial user-visible divergence: not refutable.
